name: apktool - Decompile / Rebuild Android APKs
description: apktool decodes an Android APK into near-original form: smali (disassembled Dalvik bytecode), resources, AndroidManifest.xml, and assets - then rebuilds and re-signs it. Core to static analysis and to patching apps (disable root/SSL-pinning checks, inject Frida gadget, change permissions) before reinstalling.
notes:
=== DECODE ===
  apktool d <file>                 # -> ./<appname>/ (smali, res, manifest)
  apktool d <file> -o out -f       # custom dir, force overwrite
  apktool d <file> -r              # don't decode resources (faster)

=== INSPECT ===
  cat out/AndroidManifest.xml      # permissions, exported components, debuggable
  grep -rn 'http://' out/smali     # cleartext endpoints, secrets
  ls out/smali*/                   # disassembled classes

=== PATCH + REBUILD ===
  # edit smali (e.g. force isRooted() to return 0, bypass pinning)
  apktool b out -o patched.apk

=== RE-SIGN (required to install) ===
  keytool -genkey -v -keystore k.ks -alias a -keyalg RSA -validity 10000
  apksigner sign --ks k.ks patched.apk
  adb install -r patched.apk

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  jadx           # read Java (not smali) - easier to understand
  MobSF          # automated static+dynamic
  frida          # runtime bypass without repackaging

recommended.note: jadx to read decompiled Java alongside smali.
Frida to bypass checks at runtime instead of repackaging.
MobSF for automated static triage of the APK.

defense.why_it_works: APKs are distributable archives of Dalvik bytecode and resources; apktool reverses the packaging deterministically. Without obfuscation or integrity checks, an attacker reads the app's logic/secrets and repackages it with security checks removed.
defense.prerequisites: A copy of the target APK (public on stores or pulled via adb).
defense.impact: Exposure of endpoints/keys, and the ability to redistribute a tampered app with root/pinning/license checks disabled.
defense.detection: Not detectable on the server side from static work alone; a repackaged app can be caught at runtime by integrity/signature checks reporting home.
defense.artifacts: None in the backend from static analysis; tampered-app telemetry appears only if the app performs attestation.
defense.prevention: Code obfuscation (R8/ProGuard, DexGuard); do not embed secrets in the APK; app signing + Play Integrity / SafetyNet attestation; tamper/root detection with server-side enforcement; certificate pinning; keep trust decisions server-side.
